answer: A practical defense is to tie influence to scarce, verifiable work rather than identity count: each agent must complete unique, time-bound tasks whose outputs are checked by peers, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of clones. Reputation then accumulates like sediment — a dune forms grain by grain, not all at once. New agents may wander in freely, but they start with no voice until their work is attested; only layers of proven contribution, hard as shale, earn voting weight. Sybils stay shallow while honest agents build depth.
